51555227.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to MYOF C2D (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR Assay: SPR Assay. The Biacore 8K system instrument (GE) was used to test the binding ability of HJ445A to MYOF-C2D peptides. According to the manufacturer's procedure, the MYOF-C2D protein was first immobilized on the sensor chip (CM5) by standard amine coupling in a pH 4.0 sodium acetate buffer at a flow rate of 10 μL/min to obtain densities of 5000 response units. HJ445A dissolved in 100% DMSO (10 mM stock) was then diluted to different concentrations (2-fold dilutions between 0 and 10 μM) by running buffer (10 mM phosphate buffer, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% surfactant P20, 5% DMSO). Analytes and solvent correction were injected over channels for affinity assessment at 25 °C with a flow rate of 30 μL/min. The association time and the dissociation time were 80 and 160 s, respectively. Data analysis and binding affinities were conducted by Biacore insight evaluation software, and GraphPad Prism 8 was used to make figures.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. (A) Direct interactions of HJ445A with MYOF in MKN45 were determined by CETSA (treatment with HJ445A in MKN45 cells for 1 h). (B) The binding affinity between HJ445A and the MYOF-C2D domain was determined by SPR. The surfaces of HJ445A, 6y, and the MYOF-C2D domain are shown in green, gray, and electrostatic potential, respectively. (C) The close-up views of the binding mode of HJ445A and the MYOF-C2D domain by molecular docking. The MYOF, HJ445A, and inter-residues are shown in cartoon, green, and orange, respectively (UniProt ID Q9NZM1).
original_paragraph.Figure 4B sensorgram data: The sensorgram in Figure 4B shows the response (RU) over time (seconds) for HJ445A binding to MYOF-C2D at concentrations of 10 μM, 5 μM, 2.5 μM, 1.25 μM, 0.625 μM, 0.313 μM, and 0.156 μM. The calculated K_D (M) is 1.73E-7 ± 1.49E-8, and the R_max (RU) is 19.8.

original_paragraph.Results section: Therefore, we further illustrated the binding affinity between HJ445A with MYOF encouraged by the remarkable antitumor potency and water solubility of the candidate compound HJ445A. We found that the MYOF protein would be continuously degraded when the temperature was increased from 50.0 to 56.1 °C, while the undegraded MYOF significantly increased when 50 or 100 μM of HJ445A was added in the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) (Figure 4A). The above results demonstrated that the thermal stability of MYOF was remarkably improved after binding with HJ445A, suggesting that HJ445A is directly bound to MYOF. The SPR assay was further carried out to explore the binding affinity between HJ445A and the MYOF-C2D domain. As anticipated, HJ445A directly and reversibly bound to the C2D domain of MYOF with high affinity (K_D = 0.17 μM) (Figure 4B).
